name: Energy & Utilities
tagline: Consumption, billing and collections, AT&C losses, outages and reliability (SAIDI, SAIFI), and plant generation with capacity factor and PLF
description: Meter-reading and consumption extracts from MDM, AMI and smart-meter systems (Itron, Landis+Gyr), utility billing and collection registers from CIS and billing systems (SAP IS-U, Oracle Customer Care & Billing, Indian DISCOM billing and feeder energy-audit sheets), outage and tripping logs from OMS and substation registers for SAIDI, SAIFI and CAIDI, plant generation reports (solar and wind SCADA and inverter exports, thermal PLF reports, CEA and EIA-923 plant data), and grid data such as SMARD, ENTSO-E, EIA-930 and Grid-India (POSOCO) reports, including Indian fields such as consumer number, sanctioned load, MU, CUF and AT&C.

fields.label: Reading / interval date
fields.description: When the reading, interval or generation figure applies; the dashboard's time axis for consumption and generation files.

fields.label: Consumer / account number
fields.description: One consumer connection; repeats once per reading or bill.

fields.label: Current meter reading
fields.description: Cumulative register reading at the end of the period.

fields.label: Consumption (kWh / units)
fields.description: Energy (or gas or water) used in the reading or billing period; DISCOM 'units' are kWh.

fields.label: Load / demand (kW or MW)
fields.description: Power drawn or supplied at an instant or averaged over an interval, in kW or MW.

fields.label: Billed amount
fields.description: Amount billed for the period, including fixed and energy charges and duties.

fields.label: Arrears outstanding
fields.description: Unpaid dues carried on the bill: a balance, not a flow.

fields.label: Energy input / sent out
fields.description: Energy fed into the feeder or area, against which billed units measure losses.

fields.label: Outage duration
fields.description: How long supply was off, in minutes (IEEE 1366) or hours (many Indian reports).

fields.label: Customers on feeder
fields.description: Customers that the row's feeder or area serves, whether or not they lost supply.

fields.label: Total customers served (system)
fields.description: Customers served by the whole system, usually the same on every row.

fields.label: Number of interruptions
fields.description: Outages counted on the row, as in a feeder-month reliability report.

fields.label: Generation (energy output)
fields.description: Energy produced in the interval, in kWh, MWh or MU (million kWh).

fields.label: Irradiation (kWh/m²)
fields.description: Sunlight on the panels over the interval, in kWh/m² (irradiance in W/m² is instantaneous).

fields.label: Plant availability %
fields.description: Share of the period the plant could generate; each row should cover the same length of time.

subDomains.name: Meter readings & consumption
subDomains.description: One row per meter or consumer per reading date, interval or billing period, with readings or consumption in kWh (or gas or water units), tariff category and area.

subDomains.name: Billing, collections & energy audit
subDomains.description: One row per consumer bill (or per feeder or area per month) with billed units, billed amount, amount collected, arrears and, for energy audits, input energy.

subDomains.name: Outages & reliability
subDomains.description: One row per outage or tripping (or per feeder per month) with start and restoration times, duration, customers interrupted and cause.

subDomains.name: Plant & grid generation
subDomains.description: One row per plant, unit or source per day, hour or interval with generation, installed capacity and, for grid data, generation by source and load.

kpis.name: Consumption
kpis.definition: Energy (or gas or water) used in the period, in the unit of the consumption column (kWh for most utilities; DISCOM 'units' are kWh).
kpis.formula: Sum of consumption

variants.label: Current − previous reading
variants.caveat: No consumption column, so consumption = current − previous reading, without any meter multiplying factor.

pitfalls: kWh, MWh and MU (million kWh) differ by 1,000×; check the unit before comparing files.
HT meters' multiplying factor (CT/PT ratio) must already be applied, or consumption reads far too low.

kpis.name: Billed amount
kpis.definition: Total amount billed to consumers in the period, including fixed and energy charges and duties.
kpis.formula: Sum of billed amount

kpis.name: Collection efficiency
kpis.definition: Amount collected as a share of the amount billed in the period.
kpis.formula: Σ amount collected ÷ Σ billed amount (ratio of totals)
pitfalls: Collections include arrears paid, so efficiency can pass 100% in a month when old dues are cleared.
Subsidy due from the state counts as collected only when it is received.

kpis.name: Amount collected
kpis.definition: Payments received from consumers in the period, against current bills and arrears.
kpis.formula: Sum of amount collected

kpis.name: Average billing rate
kpis.definition: Amount billed per unit of energy billed, in currency per kWh (or per the consumption unit).
kpis.formula: Σ billed amount ÷ Σ units billed, on rows that have both
pitfalls: The billed amount usually includes fixed charges, duties and taxes, so ABR sits above the energy charge per unit.

kpis.name: AT&C loss
kpis.definition: Energy lost to technical losses, theft and unbilled use plus revenue not collected: one minus billing efficiency times collection efficiency.
kpis.formula: 1 − (Σ units billed ÷ Σ input energy) × (Σ collected ÷ Σ billed amount)

benchmark.note: Indicative: India's Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) targets AT&C losses of 12–15% for distribution utilities; many run higher.

pitfalls: Input energy, billed units and collections must cover the same feeders and period; mixing an area's input with other areas' billing distorts it.

kpis.name: Consumers
kpis.definition: Distinct consumers (or meters) with a reading or bill in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct consumer numbers

variants.label: Distinct meters
variants.caveat: No consumer column, so each meter counts as one consumer.

kpis.name: Consumption per consumer
kpis.definition: Energy used per consumer in the period; for one month this is monthly consumption per consumer.
kpis.formula: Consumption ÷ distinct consumers
pitfalls: Over a quarter or a year this is consumption per consumer for the whole period, not per month.

kpis.name: Peak demand
kpis.definition: Highest load or demand recorded in the period, in the load column's unit (kW or MW).
kpis.formula: Maximum of load
pitfalls: Hourly averages hide shorter peaks; the peak of 15-minute data reads higher than that of hourly data.

kpis.name: Load factor
kpis.definition: Average load as a share of peak load: how evenly demand is spread over the period.
kpis.formula: Average load ÷ maximum load
pitfalls: Needs evenly spaced readings (every hour or 15 minutes); gaps or mixed intervals bias the average.

kpis.name: Estimated reads
kpis.definition: Share of readings or bills not based on an actual meter reading (estimated, average, door-locked or defective-meter billing).
kpis.formula: Rows with an estimated read type ÷ rows with a read type
pitfalls: Estimated bills shift consumption between months until the next actual reading, so read consumption trends alongside this share.

kpis.name: Generation
kpis.definition: Energy produced in the period, in the unit of the generation column (kWh, MWh or MU).
kpis.formula: Sum of generation
pitfalls: Gross generation includes the plant's own auxiliary use; net (sent-out) generation does not. Compare like with like.
A cumulative counter (such as an inverter's total yield) must not be summed; use the daily figure.

kpis.name: Capacity factor
kpis.definition: Energy generated as a share of what the installed capacity could have produced running flat out for the whole period (CUF for solar and wind, PLF for thermal plants).
kpis.formula: Σ generation ÷ Σ (capacity × hours in the period)

variants.label: Generation ÷ (capacity × 24 h × days, per plant)
variants.caveat: No hours column, so each plant's hours are 24 for every calendar day from its first to its last date: right for daily or finer data, far too few for monthly totals.

variants.label: Generation ÷ (capacity × 24 h × days)
variants.caveat: No hours or plant column, so the file is read as one plant with its largest capacity, over 24 hours for every calendar day from the first to the last date.

pitfalls: Generation and capacity must share a unit (MWh with MW, kWh with kW); generation in MU (million kWh) against capacity in MW reads 1,000 times too high.
Solar CUF and thermal PLF are not comparable; compare plants of one technology.

kpis.name: Installed capacity
kpis.definition: Total installed capacity of the plants in the file, each plant counted once.
kpis.formula: Σ over plants of each plant's capacity (its largest value)

variants.label: Largest capacity
variants.caveat: No plant column, so the file is read as one plant: capacity is its largest value.

pitfalls: Capacity is a stock: it is counted once per plant, never added across days or months.
When a file lists the units of one station on separate rows, map the unit column as the plant.

kpis.name: Specific yield
kpis.definition: Energy generated per unit of installed capacity (kWh per kWp, or MWh per MW): the equivalent hours at full output.
kpis.formula: Generation ÷ installed capacity
pitfalls: It grows with the length of the period; compare equal periods.

kpis.name: Renewable share
kpis.definition: Share of generation from renewable sources (solar, wind, hydro, biomass, geothermal).
kpis.formula: Generation from renewable sources ÷ all generation
pitfalls: Large hydro counts as renewable here; Indian renewable statistics (MNRE, CEA) count only small hydro.

kpis.name: Generation vs target
kpis.definition: Generation achieved against the target or expected (P50) generation.
kpis.formula: Σ generation ÷ Σ target generation, on rows that have both

kpis.name: Solar generation
kpis.definition: Energy from solar in the period, from a grid or portfolio file with a column per source.
kpis.formula: Sum of solar generation

kpis.name: Wind generation
kpis.definition: Energy from wind in the period, onshore and offshore, from a grid or portfolio file with a column per source.
kpis.formula: Sum of wind generation (or onshore + offshore)

variants.label: Onshore + offshore
variants.caveat: No total wind column, so wind = onshore + offshore.

variants.label: Onshore only
variants.caveat: Only an onshore wind column, so any offshore wind is not included.

kpis.name: SAIDI
kpis.definition: Average outage time per customer served in the period, in the unit of the duration column.
kpis.formula: Σ customer minutes interrupted ÷ customers served
pitfalls: Customers served must be everyone on the system or feeder, not only those who lost supply.
Utilities differ on excluding momentary interruptions (under 5 minutes) and major event days; compare SAIDI only under one rule.

kpis.name: SAIFI
kpis.definition: Average number of interruptions per customer served in the period.
kpis.formula: Σ customers interrupted ÷ customers served

kpis.name: CAIDI
kpis.definition: Average outage time for each customer who lost supply: SAIDI ÷ SAIFI.
kpis.formula: Σ customer minutes interrupted ÷ Σ customers interrupted

kpis.name: Outages
kpis.definition: Outages or trippings recorded in the period.
kpis.formula: Sum of interruptions per row, or distinct outage IDs

variants.label: Rows
variants.caveat: No outage ID or interruption count, so each row counts as one outage.

kpis.name: Average outage duration
kpis.definition: Average time supply was off per outage, in the unit of the duration column.
kpis.formula: Σ outage duration ÷ outages
pitfalls: Not weighted by customers: a long outage on a small feeder counts as much as one on a large feeder (CAIDI weights by customers).

kpis.name: Customer minutes interrupted
kpis.definition: Total outage time summed over every customer who lost supply, in the unit of the duration column.
kpis.formula: Σ customer minutes, or Σ (duration × customers interrupted)

variants.label: Duration × customers interrupted
variants.caveat: No customer-minutes column, so each outage's duration × customers interrupted.

kpis.name: Customers interrupted
kpis.definition: Customers who lost supply, summed over outages (a customer cut off twice counts twice).
kpis.formula: Sum of customers interrupted

kpis.name: Unplanned outages
kpis.definition: Share of outages that were not planned or scheduled work.
kpis.formula: Outages not of a planned type ÷ outages with a type

variants.label: Not planned work ÷ outages with a cause
variants.caveat: No outage-type column, so outages whose cause is not planned work count as unplanned.

kpis.name: Outages per feeder
kpis.definition: Outages per feeder that appears in the period.
kpis.formula: Outages ÷ distinct feeders
pitfalls: Feeders with no outage do not appear in an outage log, so this is outages per affected feeder.

kpis.name: Billing efficiency
kpis.definition: Units billed as a share of the energy put into the feeder or area.
kpis.formula: Σ units billed ÷ Σ input energy, on rows that have both
pitfalls: Input energy and billed units must be in one unit (MU against kWh is a millionfold gap).

kpis.name: T&D loss
kpis.definition: Share of input energy that was never billed: technical losses plus theft and unmetered use.
kpis.formula: Σ (input energy − units billed) ÷ Σ input energy, on rows that have both

kpis.name: Energy input
kpis.definition: Energy fed into the feeders or areas in the period.
kpis.formula: Sum of input energy

kpis.name: Billed but not collected
kpis.definition: Amount billed in the period minus the amount collected; negative when old arrears were cleared.
kpis.formula: Σ billed amount − Σ amount collected

kpis.name: Arrears outstanding
kpis.definition: Unpaid dues on the latest bill date in the period (a closing balance).
kpis.formula: Σ arrears on the latest bill date (semi-additive)

variants.label: Arrears on the latest bill date
Sum of arrears
variants.caveat: No bill date, so the file is treated as one point-in-time snapshot.

pitfalls: Arrears are a balance: each period shows its latest bill date. With cycle billing spread over the month, the latest date covers only that day's consumers; use a billing-month column as the date.

kpis.name: Average utility bill
kpis.definition: Average amount of one bill.
kpis.formula: Σ billed amount ÷ bills with an amount

kpis.name: Late payments
kpis.definition: Share of paid bills paid after their due date.
kpis.formula: Bills paid after the due date ÷ bills with a payment and due date
pitfalls: Unpaid bills have no payment date and are left out, so the share of overdue bills is higher than this.

kpis.name: Average power factor
kpis.definition: Power factor weighted by the energy consumed, so large consumers count in proportion.
kpis.formula: Σ (power factor × consumption) ÷ Σ consumption, on rows with a power factor

variants.label: Average of power factor
variants.caveat: No consumption column, so this is a simple average of readings, not weighted by energy.

kpis.name: Average demand
kpis.definition: Average load or demand over the readings in the period, in kW or MW.
kpis.formula: Average of load

kpis.name: Performance ratio
kpis.definition: Solar energy generated as a share of what the panels' rated capacity would give under the measured sunlight: the plant's efficiency independent of weather.
kpis.formula: Σ generation ÷ Σ (capacity × irradiation), with kWh, kWp and kWh/m²

benchmark.note: Indicative for modern grid-connected solar PV plants.

pitfalls: Needs irradiation in kWh/m² over the same interval as generation; irradiance in W/m² (an instant) gives a meaningless ratio.
Generation in kWh needs capacity in kWp; MWh against kWp is 1,000 times off.

kpis.name: Plant availability
kpis.definition: Average share of time plants or turbines were able to generate.
kpis.formula: Mean of availability over plant-periods; this equals time-weighted availability only when each row covers the same length of time
pitfalls: Valid only when every row covers an equal time span (e.g. one plant-day).

kpis.name: Target generation
kpis.definition: Target, planned or expected (P50) generation for the period.
kpis.formula: Sum of target generation

kpis.name: Consumers billed
kpis.definition: Distinct consumers billed in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct consumer numbers

variants.label: Distinct meters
variants.caveat: No consumer column, so each meter counts as one consumer.

kpis.name: Estimated bills
kpis.definition: Share of bills not based on an actual meter reading (estimated, average, door-locked or defective-meter billing).
kpis.formula: Bills with an estimated basis ÷ bills with a basis
pitfalls: Estimated bills are trued up at the next actual reading, so billed units swing between months.

kpis.name: Peak load
kpis.definition: Highest load or output recorded in the period, in the load column's unit (kW or MW).
kpis.formula: Maximum of load

kpis.name: Average output per reading
kpis.definition: Average generation per row (interval), used to draw a power curve against wind speed or sunlight.
kpis.formula: Average of generation

kpis.name: Customers served
kpis.definition: Customers on the system or on the feeders in the file, each feeder counted once: the denominator of SAIDI and SAIFI.
kpis.formula: Total customers served, or Σ over feeders of each feeder's customers

variants.label: Each feeder's customers, summed
variants.caveat: No system total, so customers served = each feeder's customers taken once and summed; feeders without an outage in the file are left out, which overstates SAIDI and SAIFI.

variants.label: Largest customer count
variants.caveat: No system total or feeder column, so the largest customer count in the file is taken as the customers served.

charts.title: Consumption over time
charts.reason: One additive measure over continuous time: an area shows the seasonal shape of demand and its volume.

charts.title: Peak demand over time
charts.reason: The peak is a maximum, recomputed for each period and drawn as a line; peaks are never added up.

charts.title: Peak load over time
charts.reason: The peak is a maximum, recomputed for each period and drawn as a line; peaks are never added up.

charts.title: Consumption by tariff category
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across a few tariff categories (domestic, commercial, industrial, agricultural): a donut shows the sales mix.

charts.title: Consumption by area
charts.reason: One total compared across named circles, divisions or zones: sorted horizontal bars keep labels readable. Top 12 plus Others.

charts.title: Consumption per consumer by tariff
charts.reason: A ratio across tariff categories: consumption per consumer recomputed per category, with categories under 20 rows hidden.

charts.title: Average demand by hour of day
charts.reason: Twenty-four ordered hours and one average: columns show the daily load curve and when the peak falls.

charts.title: Consumers by consumption band
charts.reason: How consumption is spread: consumers per band of consumption show the slab structure and the few heavy users.

charts.title: Estimated reads by area
charts.reason: Where meter reading is weakest: the recomputed share of estimated reads per area, sorted, areas under 30 rows hidden.

charts.title: Billed vs collected
charts.reason: Two amounts in one currency on one axis: the gap between the lines is the period's shortfall or arrears recovery.

charts.title: Collection efficiency over time
charts.reason: A ratio recomputed from collected and billed totals in each period, drawn as a line and never averaged.

charts.title: Billed amount by tariff category
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across a few tariff categories: a donut shows which consumers carry the revenue.

charts.title: Collection efficiency by area
charts.reason: A ratio compared across areas: the recomputed collection efficiency per circle or division, sorted, with areas under 30 rows hidden.

charts.title: Average billing rate by tariff
charts.reason: Revenue per unit across tariff categories shows cross-subsidy: industrial and commercial consumers usually pay more per kWh than domestic and agricultural ones.

charts.title: AT&C loss by feeder
charts.reason: Where energy and revenue are lost: AT&C loss recomputed per feeder from its own input, billing and collections, worst first.

charts.title: Area billing scorecard
charts.reason: Units, billing, collections, efficiency and rate per area side by side: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

charts.title: Outages over time
charts.reason: A count of events per period: columns show whether interruptions are rising, and the monsoon or storm months stand out.

charts.title: SAIDI over time
charts.reason: An index recomputed from customer minutes and customers served in each period, drawn as a line.

charts.title: Customer minutes by cause (Pareto)
charts.reason: A few causes usually account for most lost customer minutes: columns per cause with the cumulative share show what to fix first.

charts.title: Outages by feeder
charts.reason: Which feeders trip most: sorted bars of outages per feeder, top 15 plus Others.

charts.title: Outages by type
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across a few outage types (planned, unplanned, momentary): a donut shows the mix.

charts.title: Outages by hour of day
charts.reason: Twenty-four ordered hours: columns show whether trippings follow the evening peak load or daytime work.

charts.title: Feeder reliability
charts.reason: Several reliability measures per feeder: a sortable table ranks feeders by frequency, duration or customers hit.

charts.title: Generation over time
charts.reason: One additive measure over continuous time: an area shows seasonal output and its volume.

charts.title: Capacity factor over time
charts.reason: A ratio recomputed from generation and capacity in each period, drawn as a line and never averaged.

charts.title: Generation vs target
charts.reason: Actual and target in one unit on one axis: the gap between the lines is the shortfall or surplus each period.

charts.title: Generation by source over time
charts.reason: Sources are parts of total generation: stacked columns show both the total and the changing mix.

charts.title: Solar and wind generation
charts.reason: Two variable sources in one unit: stacked areas show how they complement each other across seasons.

charts.title: Generation by plant
charts.reason: One total compared across named plants or units: sorted horizontal bars, top 12 plus Others.

charts.title: Generation by source
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across a few sources: a donut shows the generation mix at a glance.

charts.title: Capacity factor by plant
charts.reason: A ratio compared across plants: the recomputed capacity factor per plant, sorted, plants with under a week of rows hidden.

charts.title: Output by wind speed
charts.reason: The turbine power curve: average output per wind-speed band, in band order, shows cut-in, rated output and any under-performance.

charts.title: Plant scorecard
charts.reason: Output, capacity and efficiency per plant side by side: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

pitfalls: Units decide everything: kWh, MWh and MU (million kWh) differ by 1,000×, as do kW and MW; check consumption, generation and capacity columns before comparing.
Collection efficiency, AT&C loss, capacity factor, SAIDI and SAIFI are recomputed from totals for every period and group; never average row-level percentages.
Arrears and installed capacity are stocks, not flows: they are taken at the latest date or once per plant, never added across months.
SAIDI and SAIFI need the customers served by the whole system or feeder, not only those who lost supply, and one rule for momentary interruptions and major event days.
Estimated (average) bills move consumption between months until the next actual reading; read consumption trends alongside the estimated-read share.
Large hydro counts as renewable here; Indian renewable statistics (MNRE, CEA) count only small hydro.
